html:
SMTO-TSK-0054 — The Agent planned a step SMTO can't run

GUID: e136cea0-7bc4-4530-8b28-e7a2d6785121
Slug: dependency-node-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent planned a set of steps, but one of them used a tool that isn't available here or included settings only SMTO itself may set. SMTO rejected the plan, so none of its steps ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Agent tries again with a different plan; it is told about this problem automatically. The Agent usually corrects an unsupported step on its next attempt.
  2. If the task ends with this error, send a message asking the Agent to continue and do the work one step at a time. None of the planned steps ran, so asking again won't repeat any work.
  3. If the step needs a particular tool, select Capabilities under the message box and make sure that tool is turned on, and that the right Gateway is selected, before you ask again. The Agent can only plan steps with tools that are turned on for this task.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's next steps start and show results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will likely be planned the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A schedule_activities (dependency graph) node names a tool that is neither an available concrete capability nor ask_user, or its arguments include reserved _smto fields such as a completion declaration.

What this means

  • A scheduled activity names neither an available concrete capability nor ask_user, or attempts to inject reserved _smto argument fields. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A scheduled activity names neither an available concrete capability nor ask_user, or attempts to inject reserved _smto argument fields.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect each node's exact capability and argument names against the current catalog and reserved-field boundary.

How to fix it

  • Every schedule_activities node must name a tool present in the run's capability catalog (or ask_user) and must not carry _smto* arguments; task completion is declared after the graph settles, not inside a node. The rejection is returned to the model as a dependency_validation result; if a model repeatedly emits such nodes, review the enabled capabilities for the run and the model in use.
  • Use current concrete tools or ask_user and remove reserved internal argument fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every accepted node is a supported concrete operation with ordinary public arguments.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
